t: What remains of St Olave Old Jewry is a tower and a west wall, standing between Old Jewry and Ironmonger Lane. The church burned in the Great Fire of 1666, was rebuilt by the office of Sir Christopher Wren, and was demolished in 1887 apart from those two pieces. Several notable people were buried here. Maurice Greene was a composer and organist, and a friend of Handel. John Boydell was an engraver, publisher and Lord Mayor in 1790. George Nicol was bookseller to George III and worked on Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery.
